title: Model entry requirements: pinning, runtime interoperability, and acceptance gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Clarify the precise requirements, acceptance gates, and rollout expectations for ingesting new open-source model weights into the Redwood model catalog. Focus areas: version pin semantics, runtime compatibility annotations, required evals, and automated guardrails that enable safe unpinned entry. This PRD addendum aims to reduce ambiguity in intake reviews and make the gating automated where possible.
scope: Applies to all new open-model submissions and repackaged community variants that request public catalog listing. Does NOT change internal enterprise/private onboarding flows. Covers metadata schema additions, mandatory eval checks, pinning options presented to submitters, and runtime compatibility signals surfaced via the catalog API and Console.
out_of_scope: Private deployment-only models, model retraining, or licensing negotiations. Major UX redesign of the Console listing page (small UI additions only).
requirements: Every inbound model must declare a canonical version identifier (semver or commit hash) and a declared set of runtime features it depends on (KV-cache semantics, flash-attention kernels, quantization level).
Pinning options: submitter chooses one of three initial modes at intake: HARD_PIN, SOFT_PIN, or UNPINNED. Each mode maps to documented runtime guarantees and rollback behavior.

Compatibility annotation: model submitters must populate a compatibility field listing supported backends (e.g., triton-v2, xla-gpu, openblas-cpu), minimum runtime version, and an expected max sequence length. The intake UI should validate format but not assert correctness beyond syntactic checks.

Eval requirements: mandatory baseline eval set must include throughput profile (tokens/sec at 4 sequence lengths), latency p50/p95 under 4 load shapes, and a quality benchmark (end-to-end task metric) with pass thresholds defined per task family.

Automated sanity checks: ingest pipeline runs a quick smoke inference that validates 1) model starts and responds to a truncated prompt within Xs, 2) KV cache correctness for a short prefix, 3) tokenization roundtrip for common tokenizer names. Failures flag the submission as BLOCKED.

Catalog API contract: newly-accepted entries must expose metadata fields `version_pin`, `compatibility_flags`, and `runtime_hints`. API consumers must be able to request only HARD_PIN models via query param.
Console and SDK: Console shows pin state and recommended fallback variants; SDK includes helper to opt into fallback behavior when a requested pin is unavailable.

Rollback and fallback policy: For SOFT_PIN and UNPINNED entries, runtime should automatically route to next-compatible pinned variant under overload or known regressions. HARD_PIN implies strict routing and capacity reservation is required for Dedicated customers.
Documentation: update public intake docs and the developer-facing pinning explainer with examples and decision matrix.
Security: if a model requires non-default kernel-level features or native extensions, security_review_required must be set to true at intake and a security review ticket created.
Telemetry: ingestion events must capture declared pin mode, result of automated sanity checks, and final admission decision for auditing.
tradeoffs: Requiring more metadata reduces risk at serving time but increases friction for submitters; to mitigate we provide a lightweight default template for community contributors. HARD_PIN increases operational cost (reserved capacity) and restricts automatic fallbacks; however it prevents silent quality regressions for critical workloads. For UNPINNED entries, we accept higher variability but require stricter eval thresholds and monitored rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated in Console + API so submitters can select HARD_PIN / SOFT_PIN / UNPINNED and provide runtime_hints fields.
Ingest pipeline implements the three automated sanity checks (startup latency, KV-cache smoke, tokenizer roundtrip) and records results in telemetry.
Catalog API returns the new metadata fields and a `pin_mode` enum; sample queries for filtering by pin_mode succeed in integration tests.
Eval pipeline runs a baseline set and marks models that fail quality/latency thresholds as BLOCKED; test stubs simulate failures in CI.
Documentation pages (intake guide, pin semantics, and runtime hints) published in Confluence with at least one example per pin mode.
Console UI surfaces pin state for model entries and a help tooltip explaining operational implications; UX review approval recorded.
Security review flag is created automatically when kernel/native flags are present; a stub security ticket is created in the onboarding flow for testing.
A canary rollout path is defined: new unpinned entries must run in discovery channel for 72 hours with no >5% regression signal before being eligible for catalog listing.

Automated rollback policy is codified: if live quality signal drops by threshold (configurable) the runtime triggers an automated fallback to pinned variant and creates an incident note in the model entry audit log.
All acceptance criteria have corresponding integration tests or QA checks in the release checklist.
All dates and fields in this ticket match the Console and API swagger examples linked in attachments.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): API + intake form changes behind feature flag; implement sanity checks and telemetry. Phase 2 (1 week): Console UI display and docs. Phase 3 (2 weeks): Eval gating integration, canary rollout for UNPINNED entries, and telemetry dashboards. Gate to GA is passing the canary with no high-severity regressions and security review flow validated.
test_plan: Unit tests for metadata parsing, integration tests for API responses, e2e test that exercises intake->ingest->catalog listing, QA script to inject a model that fails KV-cache smoke to verify BLOCKED path, and load test that verifies pinned routing under simulated capacity constraints.
